Choose the option that correctly defines Full size.
o: a triangular instrument with fixed angles used with the T-square to draw vertical and inclined lines
a named level in a CAD drawing that groups related objects for control and printing
a scale of one to one in which the drawing equals the object
the curve of points equidistant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line
items.s: Full size: a scale of one to one in which the drawing equals the object. The other options describe Layer, Parabola, Set square.

items.q: Front view is best described as
o: a pictorial drawing in which parallel lines converge at vanishing points
a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes
the view showing the length and height of an object
a curved template used to draw smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass
items.s: Front view: the view showing the length and height of an object. The other options describe French curve, Perspective drawing, Leader line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Compass?
o: the instrument used to draw circles and arcs of chosen radius
a line meeting another at exactly ninety degrees
a CAD setting that makes the cursor lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
a projection in which the view from the left is placed on the right of the front view
items.s: Compass: the instrument used to draw circles and arcs of chosen radius. The other options describe Perpendicular, Object snap, First angle projection.

items.q: The statement “a model that represents an object by its bounding faces without interior volume” describes which of the following?
o: Orthographic projection
Surface model
Hidden detail line
Drawing board
items.s: Surface model is a model that represents an object by its bounding faces without interior volume.

items.q: All of the following belong to Drawing instruments and materials EXCEPT
o: Set square
T-square
Drawing board
Auxiliary view
items.s: Every other option belongs to Drawing instruments and materials. “Auxiliary view” belongs to Orthographic projection, not Drawing instruments and materials.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Oblique drawing?
o: the instrument used to measure and set out angles
a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen
a model that represents an object only by its edges and vertices
a pictorial drawing in which the front face is drawn true shape and depth is drawn at an angle
items.s: Oblique drawing: a pictorial drawing in which the front face is drawn true shape and depth is drawn at an angle. The other options describe Protractor, Third angle projection, Wireframe model.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Isometric scale.
o: the curve of points whose difference of distances from two fixed foci is constant
the circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides
the flat pattern obtained by unfolding the surfaces of a solid
the scale that reduces true lengths to isometric lengths by a factor of about 0.816
items.s: Isometric scale: the scale that reduces true lengths to isometric lengths by a factor of about 0.816. The other options describe Hyperbola, Surface development, Incircle.

items.q: Ellipse is best described as
o: the instrument used to draw circles and arcs of chosen radius
a line showing where an object has been imaginarily cut to reveal its interior
a closed curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed foci add to a constant
a named level in a CAD drawing that groups related objects for control and printing
items.s: Ellipse: a closed curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed foci add to a constant. The other options describe Layer, Section line, Compass.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Perpendicular?
o: a line meeting another at exactly ninety degrees
the view showing the length and height of an object
the actual outline of a face obtained by projecting it onto a parallel plane
a CAD setting that makes the cursor lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
items.s: Perpendicular: a line meeting another at exactly ninety degrees. The other options describe Object snap, Front view, True shape.

items.q: The statement “a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature” describes which of the following?
o: Surface model
Centre line
Wireframe model
Perspective drawing
items.s: Centre line is a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature.

items.q: All of the following belong to Solid modelling and CAD EXCEPT
o: Leader line
Wireframe model
Solid model
Surface model
items.s: Every other option belongs to Solid modelling and CAD. “Leader line” belongs to Drawing conventions, not Solid modelling and CAD.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Parabola?
o: the curve of points equidistant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line
the view showing the length and height of an object
the actual outline of a face obtained by projecting it onto a parallel plane
evenly spaced thin lines drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a sectional view
items.s: Parabola: the curve of points equidistant from a fixed point and a fixed straight line. The other options describe Front view, Hatching, True shape.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Representative fraction.
o: the view from above showing length and breadth
a CAD setting that makes the cursor lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
a CAD setting that constrains the cursor to horizontal or vertical movement
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the object
items.s: Representative fraction: the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the object. The other options describe Object snap, Plan, Orthographic snap.

items.q: Dimension line is best described as
o: a thin line terminated by arrowheads that carries a measurement on a drawing
the instrument used to transfer and step off measurements along a line
the flat wooden or plastic surface on which a drawing sheet is pinned and worked
the line or arc that divides a line or an angle into two equal parts
items.s: Dimension line: a thin line terminated by arrowheads that carries a measurement on a drawing. The other options describe Bisector, Drawing board, Divider.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Leader line?
o: a curved template used to draw smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass
a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes
the curved side surface of a cylinder or cone, excluding the ends
a pencil graded by hardness, with H grades for construction lines and B grades for visible outlines
items.s: Leader line: a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes. The other options describe French curve, Lateral surface, Drawing pencil.

items.q: The statement “a drawing of a single component showing all dimensions needed to make it” describes which of the following?
o: Cone development
Circumcircle
Incircle
Detail drawing
items.s: Detail drawing is a drawing of a single component showing all dimensions needed to make it.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Layer?
o: a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used
the curve of points whose difference of distances from two fixed foci is constant
a named level in a CAD drawing that groups related objects for control and printing
the circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides
items.s: Layer: a named level in a CAD drawing that groups related objects for control and printing. The other options describe Incircle, Isometric drawing, Hyperbola.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Circumcircle.
o: the curved side surface of a cylinder or cone, excluding the ends
a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature
a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes
the circle that passes through all three vertices of a triangle
items.s: Circumcircle: the circle that passes through all three vertices of a triangle. The other options describe Leader line, Centre line, Lateral surface.

items.q: French curve is best described as
o: a continuous thick line used for the edges of an object that can be seen
a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature
a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen
a curved template used to draw smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass
items.s: French curve: a curved template used to draw smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass. The other options describe Visible outline, Third angle projection, Centre line.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hatching?
o: evenly spaced thin lines drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a sectional view
a CAD setting that constrains the cursor to horizontal or vertical movement
a closed figure with all sides and all interior angles equal
an instrument with a fixed stock and blade used to draw horizontal lines and to guide set squares
items.s: Hatching: evenly spaced thin lines drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a sectional view. The other options describe T-square, Orthographic snap, Regular polygon.

items.q: The statement “a view projected on a plane inclined to the principal planes to show a slanted face truly” describes which of the following?
o: Surface model
Computer aided design
Assembly drawing
Auxiliary view
items.s: Auxiliary view is a view projected on a plane inclined to the principal planes to show a slanted face truly.

items.q: All of the following belong to Pictorial drawing EXCEPT
o: Oblique drawing
Isometric scale
Isometric drawing
Visible outline
items.s: Every other option belongs to Pictorial drawing. “Visible outline” belongs to Drawing conventions, not Pictorial drawing.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Plain scale?
o: a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes
a drawing showing several components fitted together in their working positions
a view showing the object from the front or the side, giving height
a scale that reads to one unit and one decimal place of the unit
items.s: Plain scale: a scale that reads to one unit and one decimal place of the unit. The other options describe Elevation, Assembly drawing, Leader line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Surface development.
o: a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used
a CAD setting that constrains the cursor to horizontal or vertical movement
the circle that passes through all three vertices of a triangle
the flat pattern obtained by unfolding the surfaces of a solid
items.s: Surface development: the flat pattern obtained by unfolding the surfaces of a solid. The other options describe Circumcircle, Isometric drawing, Orthographic snap.

items.q: Section line is best described as
o: a view showing the object from the front or the side, giving height
a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen
a line showing where an object has been imaginarily cut to reveal its interior
a pictorial drawing in which parallel lines converge at vanishing points
items.s: Section line: a line showing where an object has been imaginarily cut to reveal its interior. The other options describe Third angle projection, Perspective drawing, Elevation.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Cone development?
o: an instrument with a fixed stock and blade used to draw horizontal lines and to guide set squares
a thin line with an arrowhead that connects a note or dimension to the feature it describes
the flat sector obtained by unfolding the curved surface of a cone
a triangular instrument with fixed angles used with the T-square to draw vertical and inclined lines
items.s: Cone development: the flat sector obtained by unfolding the curved surface of a cone. The other options describe Leader line, T-square, Set square.

items.q: The statement “a projection in which the view from the left is placed on the right of the front view” describes which of the following?
o: First angle projection
Assembly drawing
True shape
Regular polygon
items.s: First angle projection is a projection in which the view from the left is placed on the right of the front view.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Hyperbola?
o: a scale that reads to one unit and one decimal place of the unit
a scale that allows measurement to two decimal places by using similar triangles
the curve of points whose difference of distances from two fixed foci is constant
a pencil graded by hardness, with H grades for construction lines and B grades for visible outlines
items.s: Hyperbola: the curve of points whose difference of distances from two fixed foci is constant. The other options describe Plain scale, Drawing pencil, Diagonal scale.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines T-square.
o: a model that represents an object only by its edges and vertices
a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen
a named level in a CAD drawing that groups related objects for control and printing
an instrument with a fixed stock and blade used to draw horizontal lines and to guide set squares
items.s: T-square: an instrument with a fixed stock and blade used to draw horizontal lines and to guide set squares. The other options describe Layer, Wireframe model, Third angle projection.

items.q: Solid model is best described as
o: a closed curve traced by a point whose distances from two fixed foci add to a constant
the flat wooden or plastic surface on which a drawing sheet is pinned and worked
a short-dashed line used for edges that are hidden from view
a model that represents an object with complete volume and mass properties
items.s: Solid model: a model that represents an object with complete volume and mass properties. The other options describe Ellipse, Hidden detail line, Drawing board.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Break line?
o: a thin irregular line showing that part of a long object has been omitted
the view showing the length and height of an object
a model that represents an object by its bounding faces without interior volume
a pictorial drawing in which the front face is drawn true shape and depth is drawn at an angle
items.s: Break line: a thin irregular line showing that part of a long object has been omitted. The other options describe Front view, Oblique drawing, Surface model.

items.q: The statement “a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen” describes which of the following?
o: Incircle
Cone development
Third angle projection
Compass
items.s: Third angle projection is a projection in which each view is placed on the side from which it is seen.

items.q: All of the following belong to Auxiliary views and development EXCEPT
o: Ellipse
Surface development
True shape
Lateral surface
items.s: Every other option belongs to Auxiliary views and development. “Ellipse” belongs to Geometric construction, not Auxiliary views and development.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Incircle?
o: the circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides
the curve formed where the surfaces of two solids meet
the instrument used to transfer and step off measurements along a line
a solid whose top has been cut off by a plane not parallel to its base
items.s: Incircle: the circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides. The other options describe Divider, Truncated solid, Intersection of solids.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Truncated solid.
o: a drawing showing several components fitted together in their working positions
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the object
a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used
a solid whose top has been cut off by a plane not parallel to its base
items.s: Truncated solid: a solid whose top has been cut off by a plane not parallel to its base. The other options describe Representative fraction, Assembly drawing, Isometric drawing.

items.q: Hidden detail line is best described as
o: a model that represents an object only by its edges and vertices
a pencil graded by hardness, with H grades for construction lines and B grades for visible outlines
the curve formed where the surfaces of two solids meet
a short-dashed line used for edges that are hidden from view
items.s: Hidden detail line: a short-dashed line used for edges that are hidden from view. The other options describe Intersection of solids, Wireframe model, Drawing pencil.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Regular polygon?
o: evenly spaced thin lines drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a sectional view
the instrument used to draw circles and arcs of chosen radius
a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature
a closed figure with all sides and all interior angles equal
items.s: Regular polygon: a closed figure with all sides and all interior angles equal. The other options describe Centre line, Compass, Hatching.

items.q: The statement “a triangular instrument with fixed angles used with the T-square to draw vertical and inclined lines” describes which of the following?
o: Perspective drawing
Hyperbola
Hatching
Set square
items.s: Set square is a triangular instrument with fixed angles used with the T-square to draw vertical and inclined lines.

items.q: All of the following belong to Geometric construction EXCEPT
o: Truncated solid
Circumcircle
Bisector
Perpendicular
items.s: Every other option belongs to Geometric construction. “Truncated solid” belongs to Auxiliary views and development, not Geometric construction.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Enlarging scale?
o: a scale on which the drawing is larger than the object
a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature
the curve of points whose difference of distances from two fixed foci is constant
the circle drawn inside a triangle touching all three sides
items.s: Enlarging scale: a scale on which the drawing is larger than the object. The other options describe Incircle, Hyperbola, Centre line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Diagonal scale.
o: the view showing the length and height of an object
a model that represents an object by its bounding faces without interior volume
a scale that allows measurement to two decimal places by using similar triangles
a CAD setting that makes the cursor lock onto exact points such as endpoints and centres
items.s: Diagonal scale: a scale that allows measurement to two decimal places by using similar triangles. The other options describe Surface model, Object snap, Front view.

items.q: Visible outline is best described as
o: a triangular instrument with fixed angles used with the T-square to draw vertical and inclined lines
a scale on which the drawing is smaller than the object
a continuous thick line used for the edges of an object that can be seen
a drawing of a single component showing all dimensions needed to make it
items.s: Visible outline: a continuous thick line used for the edges of an object that can be seen. The other options describe Set square, Detail drawing, Reducing scale.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Isometric drawing?
o: a short-dashed line used for edges that are hidden from view
a view projected on a plane inclined to the principal planes to show a slanted face truly
a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used
a scale that allows measurement to two decimal places by using similar triangles
items.s: Isometric drawing: a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used. The other options describe Diagonal scale, Hidden detail line, Auxiliary view.

items.q: The statement “the curve formed where the surfaces of two solids meet” describes which of the following?
o: Parabola
Drawing board
Intersection of solids
Regular polygon
items.s: Intersection of solids is the curve formed where the surfaces of two solids meet.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Computer aided design?
o: a pictorial drawing in which the three axes are set at 120 degrees and true lengths are used
the use of software to create, edit, analyse and store engineering drawings and models
the view showing the length and height of an object
an instrument with a fixed stock and blade used to draw horizontal lines and to guide set squares
items.s: Computer aided design: the use of software to create, edit, analyse and store engineering drawings and models. The other options describe Isometric drawing, T-square, Front view.

o: a curved template used to draw smooth curves that cannot be drawn with a compass
the instrument used to draw circles and arcs of chosen radius
the instrument used to measure and set out angles
the instrument used to transfer and step off measurements along a line
items.s: Protractor: the instrument used to measure and set out angles. The other options describe Divider, French curve, Compass.

items.q: “a line showing where an object has been imaginarily cut to reveal its interior” is the definition of
o: Break line
Dimension line
Section line
Leader line
items.s: Section line is a line showing where an object has been imaginarily cut to reveal its interior.

items.q: The correct meaning of Enlarging scale is
o: a scale on which the drawing is larger than the object
a scale of one to one in which the drawing equals the object
the ratio of a length on the drawing to the corresponding length on the object
a scale that reads to one unit and one decimal place of the unit
items.s: Enlarging scale: a scale on which the drawing is larger than the object. The other options describe Full size, Representative fraction, Plain scale.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Detail drawing.
o: a model that represents an object only by its edges and vertices
a drawing of a single component showing all dimensions needed to make it
a drawing showing several components fitted together in their working positions
a model that represents an object with complete volume and mass properties
items.s: Detail drawing: a drawing of a single component showing all dimensions needed to make it. The other options describe Solid model, Assembly drawing, Wireframe model.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Dimension line.
o: a long-and-short dash line marking the axis or centre of a symmetrical feature
evenly spaced thin lines drawn at an angle across a cut surface in a sectional view
a thin irregular line showing that part of a long object has been omitted
a thin line terminated by arrowheads that carries a measurement on a drawing
items.s: Dimension line: a thin line terminated by arrowheads that carries a measurement on a drawing. The other options describe Hatching, Centre line, Break line.
